description: The only way to give this round's answer when it is a plan. Fill the fields and call it; the platform builds and stores the answer from them. Do not write the answer as text.

parameters.plan: The plan, with the fields below.
parameters.plan.stages: array of {stageId, title, description?}; a task names its stage by stageId.
parameters.plan.tasks: array of {taskId, stageId?, title, requirementLevel, taskKind, disposition, scope, executionIntent?, plannedFiles?}; requirementLevel required|optional; taskKind work|gate; disposition active|deferred|cancelled|superseded; executionIntent plan_only|request_execution (work only); scope {kind:"goal"}|{kind:"stage",stageId}|{kind:"module",stageId,moduleRef}. Each stage has exactly one required stage gate (taskKind "gate", scope {kind:"stage",stageId}); it covers only that stage's stage- or module-scoped work, and goal-scoped work counts for no stage gate, so scope each stage's work to its stage. The plan has exactly one required goal gate.
parameters.plan.assignments: array of {taskId, role, instruction}; request_execution needs exactly one AVAILABLE-role assignment; a gate carries neither assignment nor executionIntent. When the person keeps a decision for themselves, that task's instruction says to report and wait for the reply, any goalCardDrafts completion says the person has decided, and no check stands in for the person's decision.
parameters.plan.obligations: array of {obligationId, title, requirementLevel, taskIds, verificationRequirements}; each entry is {requirementId, requirementLevel, kind, description, requiredReadPaths?} with kind from the policy; a required obligation meets the policy minimum.
parameters.plan.executionDag: {dependsOn:[{taskId, dependsOnId, requires:{kind, label}}]}; requires.kind is "artifact", "environment-revision" or "gate-result"; keep the DAG acyclic.
parameters.plan.taskRelations: optional array of {fromTaskId, toTaskId, kind, note}; kind is "coordination" or "expected_dependency"; advisory only.
parameters.setup: Required this round, which has no adopted architecture or active completion policy; it has exactly architecture, completionPolicy and checks.
parameters.setup.architecture: architecture: {baselineId, description, constraints:[{name, scope}], catalog:{dependencies:[{from, to, reason}], modules:[{moduleId, name, responsibility, paths, interfaces:[{id, description, paths}]}], containment?}}; bare moduleIds; containment only when proven, omitted means unknown, the empty {parentOf:[]} means flat.
parameters.setup.completionPolicy: completionPolicy: {requirementKinds:[...], minimumRequiredRequirementsPerObligation:N}; copy the effective policy's kinds, include "witness" for a witness requirement, and when none is shown propose the smallest real policy, never an empty one.
parameters.setup.checks: array of {checkId, kind, command, cwd, timeoutMs, taskIds}; kind is "static" or "dynamic"; taskIds is "all" or real ids; every required non-reviewer/witness requirement needs a matching-kind check. The command runs in bash, where double quotes eat one backslash: put variables in double quotes and regexes in single quotes; wrap a node -e or python -c script in single quotes and use double quotes inside it.
parameters.goalCardDrafts: Only when this request has no goal: at least one {objective, completion, autonomy, screening?} draft; objective one sentence, completion a non-empty array of checkable criteria, autonomy "every_step" or "after_plan_confirmation"; screening {modules, size, conflictsWith, dependsOn, urgency, suggestedPosition, note} with bare moduleId/goalId, size "small"|"medium"|"large"|"unknown", urgency "high"|"normal"|"low", suggestedPosition null or integer >= 0, note at most 512 UTF-8 bytes.
parameters.planDraftIndex: Only when this request has no goal: zero-based index of the goalCardDrafts entry this plan is for.
